headline: Democrats' sweep of Congress sends the Dow up 3% and oil down 8%, but chips sink 3%
summary: Futures fell as much as 1–2.5% overnight as early results showed Democrats taking both chambers, then reversed once Trump accepted the outcome; the S&P 500 was up about 1.8% by early afternoon and closed 1.6% higher, with the Dow posting its best day since April 2025. Advancers led on both exchanges and volume ran above average, but the AI trade split hard: cash-rich Big Tech platforms rallied while chipmakers and data-center builders sold off. Consumer discretionary gained about 4.3% while energy dropped about 4.7% with crude.
drivers: Democrats won majorities in the House and Senate, and Trump said he would work with them, taking a contested-count tail risk off the table; strategists cited gridlock as historically friendly to stocks. The VIX fell about 20% to 16.61, its lowest close in weeks, and the Dow added 1,569 points.
Big Tech rallies on a slower data-center buildout

Microsoft rose about 6.7%, Amazon 6.1%, Apple about 5.3% and Alphabet 3.2% as investors bet that state-level limits on data centers would ease capex and cash demands on the hyperscalers; Goldman flagged moratorium risk for roughly 45% of planned US capacity after Democratic wins in Texas and Georgia.
AI infrastructure and chips sell off

The SOX fell 3.1% to a six-month low, with Micron down about 7% and Nvidia about 3%; Hut 8 (−23%), Vertiv (about −13%), IREN (−11%) and CoreWeave (about −10%) led data-center losers. AMD gave back most of an early 6% jump on its upbeat 2027 outlook to finish about 1% higher; Tesla and SpaceX fell more than 3% on scrutiny worries.
Oil plunges on hopes of an Iran war exit

WTI sank 8.3% to $88.12, its lowest since Aug 31 and biggest drop since April, after Vance blamed the Iran war for Republican losses and Democratic leaders pledged to end it; energy and defense stocks fell while solar jumped. Lower oil pulled the 10-year yield down about 5bp to 4.90% and the dollar weakened, while ADP payrolls (+86K) beat and ISM services (54.5) was steady.
week: Three sessions in, the S&P 500 is up 1.4%, the Nasdaq 1.2%, the Dow 3.1% and the Russell 2000 1.6%, though the Nasdaq-100 remains in a correction and the SOX at a six-month low; the backdrop is a Fed on hold at 3.75–4% with December hike risk still priced and crude down sharply this week.
watch: Next: Qualcomm slid about 4–5% after hours on a light earnings outlook as handset chip sales fell 26%, and Arm also reported after the close; the October jobs report on Friday, Nov 6 is the main data test for the Fed.
